data.gender_notes: Eliodoro is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew name Elio (my God) and dore (light). In the Bible, Eliodor is the name of a high priest who served in the Temple in Jerusalem during the reign of King Joash. The name Eliodoro carries the meaning “My God is light” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Eliodoro usually hope their child will grow to embody my god is light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Signifies the presence of God's light in one's life.
data.etymology: Eliodoro belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “My God is light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Eliodoro total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: אליהודורו
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא אור, מתנת אלוהים, או שוער האור
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אליהודורו הוא שם שמקורו ביוונית ומורכב משני שמות: אליוס (אלוהים) והדורוס (מתנה או שוער). הוא מתורגם לאור האל או מתנת האל. השם משלב את המושגים של האל הבורא והאור הרוחני.

in_greek.name: Ελιόδωρος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ελιόδωρος προέρχεται από τα ελληνικά και σημαίνει δωρον του Θεου (δωρον του Θεου) ή φωστηρ (αυτό που φέρνει φως). Ο Ελιόδωρος είναι σύνθετο όνομα από το 'ήλιος' (ελιος) και το 'δωρος' (δώρος), υπονοώντας το φως του Θεού ή το δώρο του Θεού. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόμοια ονόματα συνδέονται με έννοιες πνευματικού φωτός και θείας δωρεάς.

in_latin.name: Eliodoro
in_latin.meaning: Dei donum, lux Dei, Domini donatio
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Eliodoro derivatur ex Graecis vocibus et significat donum Dei, lux Dei, seu Domini donatio. In traditione Christiana, nomen hoc reflectit relationem inter Deum et hominem, dono divino et lumine spirituali.

in_english.name: Eliodoro
in_english.meaning: Gift of God, God's light, or Door of light
in_english.long_meaning: Eliodoro is a Christian name derived from Greek roots, meaning 'gift of God' or 'God's light.' It combines 'elios' (God or sun) and 'doros' (gift or door), symbolizing spiritual enlightenment and divine favor. Historically, the name reflects early Christian traditions of naming children after divine attributes or blessings. Eliodoro conveys a sense of sacredness, divine presence, and illumination, resonating with Christian values of faith and redemption.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eliodoro has its roots in the rich history and culture of the Hebrew people. It is derived from the Hebrew words El (my God) and dore (light). The name reflects the faith, hope, and trust the Hebrew people had in their God during Biblical times. The name continues to hold significance in the contemporary Christian world as a reminder of the faithful connection between God and his people.
data.spiritual_significance: Eliodoro is a name that embodies the spiritual qualities of faith and light. In the Bible, the name is associated with Eliodor, a high priest who served in the Temple in Jerusalem during the reign of King Joash. The name is a reminder that even in the darkest of times, God is our light and our guide. It also reflects the deep faith and trust that the Hebrew people had in their God. Today, the name is a source of inspiration for Christians seeking to live their lives in faith and trust in God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Eliodoro means "my God is gold" in Hebrew. This name signifies a deep and unwavering faith in God, the belief that the true wealth and value come from the divine, and a life dedicated to the pursuit of spiritual riches.

historical_references.reference: Eliodorus was a high-ranking Roman official during the rule of Emperor Nero in Rome. He is known for his involvement in the persecution of early Christians, and was one of the chief accusers of St. Peter at his trial in AD 64.

Eliodorus was a Greek bishop in the early Christian Church, possibly in Sicily around the 5th century AD. He is venerated as a saint and is the patron saint of Messina, Italy. Little is known about his life beyond his name and the fact that he was a bishop.

It has been featured in Italian literature, such as the novel 'I Lombardi' by Alessandro Manzoni. In art history, the name Eliodoro is associated with the famous sculpture 'Eliodoro and Mercury' by Gian Lorenzo Bernini. On social media platforms like Facebook and Instagram, the name Eliodoro is used as a unique identifier for individuals, while on Wikipedia, it is a search term for accessing information about the name's origins and historical significance.
